text:
No single treaty ended World War II, and the Treaty of Versailles (1919) ended World War I, so the earlier statement was wrong.

WWII ended through surrender instruments: Germany's unconditional surrender (signed May 7 and ratified May 8, 1945) and Japan's Instrument of Surrender (September 2, 1945). Formal peace treaties came later:

- Paris Peace Treaties (1947): Italy, Romania, Hungary, Bulgaria, Finland.
- Treaty of San Francisco (1951, in force 1952): Japan and most Allied powers.
- Treaty on the Final Settlement with Respect to Germany, or "Two Plus Four" (1990): the final German settlement, with no separate peace treaty ever signed.
